claims.claim_text: Rocket Lab is a federal contractor with the U.S. Department of War (formerly DoD), NASA, DARPA, and the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), including SDA Tranche 3 contract signed December 2025. Federal-agency dollars should be visible in USAspending.

Electron launched 21 times in 2025; cumulative 75 successful missions and over 200 spacecraft deployed through Dec 31, 2025; second-most frequently launched orbital rocket in 2025; revenue $601.8M FY2025 (up 38% YoY).

Named commercial spacecraft customers include Blacksky Holdings, Capella Space, Planet, OHB, Synspective, Canon, Kineis, and MDA Corporation (Feb 2022 contract for 17 spacecraft buses). Material commercial relationships should appear in counterparty 10-Ks where commercial counterparties are EDGAR filers.

Rocket Lab has extensive proprietary technology including 3D-printed Rutherford engines, Photon spacecraft, Archimedes engine for Neutron, optical systems, reaction wheels, star trackers, solar cells, separation systems. Claim of patent portfolio should be verifiable via USPTO.

Rocket Lab operates physical US facilities including Long Beach, CA HQ (engine production), Albuquerque, NM solar cell production (~160K sq ft, from SolAero acquisition), Stennis Space Center MS (Archimedes engine testing), Middle River, MD (composite production), Tucson, AZ (optical systems/EO-IR sensors), Wallops Island, VA (LC-2 launch complex). These are EPA-regulable industrial sites.

Rocket Lab is selected for NASA Artemis-program work (CAPSTONE lunar mission via Photon, launched 2022) and provides components used by defense primes (Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman). Material relationships should leave counterparty traces.

Neutron medium-lift launch vehicle is under construction at LC-3 Wallops; payload capacity 13,000 kg reusable to LEO. Subsequent event Jan 21, 2026: Neutron Stage 1 tank qualification testing FAILURE (ruptured during hydrostatic pressure trial), impacting launch schedule. Securities class action (Feb 2025) alleges misstatements re Neutron progress.

Rocket Lab signed a Direct Funding Agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce that restricts share buybacks and dividends. Such an agreement (likely CHIPS Act / OSC industrial-base program) should be visible in USAspending as a federal financial assistance (grant/cooperative agreement).
